t: Prior period items and changes in accounting policies are covered by:
e: AS 5 deals with net profit or loss for the period, prior period items and changes in accounting policies.

t: Disclosure of transactions with subsidiaries, KMP and their relatives is required by:
e: AS 18 governs related party disclosures.

t: Applying the same depreciation method from year to year satisfies the:
e: Consistency requires the same accounting methods to be followed from period to period for comparability.

t: GAAP stands for:
e: Accounting principles are collectively known as Generally Accepted Accounting Principles.

t: A company has capital of ₹500 crore and liabilities of ₹900 crore. It then borrows a further ₹100 crore. Total assets after the borrowing are:
e: Assets = Capital + Liabilities = 500 + (900 + 100) = ₹1,500 crore.

t: Appointment of auditors generally is covered by which section of the Companies Act, 2013?
e: Section 139 deals with appointment of auditors; sub-section (7) covers Government companies.

t: Net Written Premium is ₹1,000 crore, opening Unearned Premium Reserve ₹450 crore and closing UPR ₹520 crore. Net Earned Premium is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). NEP = NWP − (closing UPR − opening UPR) = 1,000 − 70 = ₹930 crore.

t: Section 139(7) of the Companies Act, 2013 applies to:
o: Government companies and companies owned or controlled by the Central or State Government
e: Section 139(7) covers auditor appointment for Government companies and companies controlled by Central/State Government.

t: Purchase of a new office building by a regional office is classified as:
e: Expenditure on acquiring long-term assets is capital expenditure (CAPEX); day-to-day running costs are OPEX.

t: FIFO, a method of inventory valuation, stands for:
e: FIFO assumes the earliest purchased items are issued first; LIFO is Last-In, First-Out.

t: Interest credited by the bank, not yet recorded in the cash book, has the effect of:
o: Increasing the pass book balance relative to the cash book
Decreasing the pass book balance relative to the cash book
e: Interest credited by the bank raises the pass book balance until the cash book is updated.

t: A cheque issued to a supplier was omitted from the cash book. In the BRS this is classified as:
o: An error committed by the firm
An error committed by the bank
e: Omission of a transaction in the cash book is an error of the firm; it decreases the pass book relative to the cash book.

t: Cash book balance ₹1,50,000. Cheques issued but not presented ₹40,000; cheques deposited not yet cleared ₹70,000; amount directly deposited by a customer ₹15,000 not in cash book. Pass book balance is:

topic: Supplement: Insurance Act and IRDAI Rules
t: Under IRDAI investment norms, a general insurer must invest in Central Government securities not less than:
e: The pattern requires at least 20% in Central Government securities, at least 30% in Central/State/other approved securities (including the 20%), and at least 15% in housing and infrastructure.

t: Under Ind AS 117 the general measurement model for insurance contracts is also known as the:
e: The general measurement model (Building Block Approach) uses fulfilment cash flows plus the contractual service margin.

t: The CFO wishes to switch from the 50% method to the 1/365 (unexpired period) method of providing UPR. What is required?
o: No approval, as both methods are permitted
Prior written approval of the Competent Authority
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Any change in the method of provisioning for UPR requires prior written approval of the Competent Authority.

t: Under Ind AS 117, the 'risk adjustment' is the compensation an insurer requires for bearing:
o: Uncertainty about the amount and timing of cash flows from non-financial risk
e: The risk adjustment reflects non-financial risk in the fulfilment cash flows.

t: Chapter II of the IRDAI AFI Regulations, 2024 contains:
o: Guiding principles for actuarial, finance and investment functions
e: Chapter I is preliminary, Chapter II guiding principles and Chapter III miscellaneous.

t: 'Net Retained Premium' is another name for:
e: Net premium, net written premium and net retained premium are the same measure: GWP less reinsurance ceded.

t: Gross Written Premium ₹5,000 crore and reinsurance ceded ₹1,500 crore. Net Written Premium is:
e: NWP = GWP − ceded = 5,000 − 1,500 = ₹3,500 crore.

t: Net Written Premium ₹3,500 crore; opening UPR ₹1,600 crore; closing UPR ₹1,750 crore. Net Earned Premium is:
Net claims paid ₹2,000 crore; net outstanding claims at year end ₹3,200 crore and at the beginning ₹3,000 crore. Net Incurred Claims are:
In computing Net Incurred Claims, net outstanding claims include:
e: Net outstanding claims include net IBNR/IBNER.

t: Provision for claims in transit as on the valuation date forms part of:
e: IBNR reserves include claims in transit, ALAE and reopened claims estimates.

t: Sundry debts, advances and receivables are placed at zero value for solvency:
o: To the extent they are of unrealisable nature
e: Sundry debts, advances and receivables are inadmissible only to the extent they are unrealisable.

t: Reinsurers' balances, other than Indian reinsurers and foreign reinsurers with branches in India, are inadmissible if outstanding beyond:
e: Other reinsurers' balances are placed at zero after 180 days; Indian/FRB balances after 365 days.

t: Deferred expenses are, for solvency margin computation:
e: Deferred expenses, furniture and fictitious assets are placed at zero value.

topic: Supplement: Insurance Act and IRDAI Rules
t: The IBNR reserve of a general insurer is determined and certified by:
e: IBNR/IBNER provisions are estimated and certified by the Appointed Actuary using actuarial methods.

t: Gross premium written in India is ₹5,000 crore and incremental premium from PMFBY is ₹200 crore. The allowable expenses of management are:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). 30% × 5,000 = 1,500 plus 15% of incremental PMFBY premium 200 = 30; total ₹1,530 crore.

t: Agents' balances and outstanding premium in India total ₹50 crore, of which ₹12 crore is older than 30 days. Admissible value for solvency is:
e: Balances beyond 30 days are placed at zero: 50 − 12 = ₹38 crore.

t: Gross Incurred Claims ₹1,500 crore with Factor B of 0.9; Net Incurred Claims ₹1,300 crore. RSM 2 is:
e: GIC × B = 1,350, higher than NIC 1,300; RSM 2 = 30% × 1,350 = ₹405 crore.

t: Required Solvency Margin is ₹2,000 crore. The minimum Available Solvency Margin needed to meet the 150% control level is:
e: ASM must be at least 1.5 × RSM = ₹3,000 crore.

t: The Required Solvency Margin is computed as the higher of RSM 1 and RSM 2:
o: For the company as a whole only
Only for lines with underwriting losses
For each specified line of business separately
e: RSM is the higher of RSM 1 and RSM 2 for each specified LOB separately, then totalled.

t: Payment for purchase of a fixed asset is classified in the cash flow statement under:
e: Acquisition and disposal of long-term assets are investing activities.

t: Section 41 of the Insurance Act 1938 prohibits:
o: Payment of any rebate of premium or commission as an inducement to buy insurance
Issue of a policy without a medical examination
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 41 bars rebating; contravention attracts a penalty of up to ₹10 lakh.

t: Net written premium of the Miscellaneous segment for the preceding twelve months is ₹2,600 crore. UPR under the percentage method is:
e: Other segments carry 50% UPR: 50% × 2,600 = ₹1,300 crore.

t: Under the percentage method, UPR for Marine Cargo is created at:
o: 50% of net written premium, like other segments
100% of net written premium, like Marine Hull
e: Only Marine Hull carries 100%; Marine Cargo falls under 'other segments' at 50%.

t: A proposal with cheque is received but underwriting is incomplete and risk has not commenced at year end. The amount is:
o: Gross direct premium of the year
Unallocated premium, shown under current liabilities
e: Premium received where risk has not commenced is unallocated premium and is a current liability.

t: Government securities held by an insurer are:
o: Not marked to market; carried at historical cost
Marked to market through the Fair Value Change Account
Marked to market through the Profit and Loss Account
e: G-secs are held-to-maturity debt securities measured at historical cost.

t: Unrealised gains on actively traded equity shares are:
o: Credited to the Profit and Loss Account
Not recognised in the Profit and Loss Account
e: Such gains go to the Fair Value Change Account under equity and are not available for distribution.

t: Real estate carried at ₹100 crore is revalued downward to ₹90 crore. The ₹10 crore reduction is:
o: Debited to the Revaluation Reserve under equity
Debited to the Fair Value Change Account
Charged to the Profit and Loss Account
e: Gains and losses from changes in the carrying amount of real estate are taken to equity under the Revaluation Reserve.

t: TDS on rentals receivable from investment property, accounted on gross basis, is shown under:
e: TDS on interest, dividends and rentals on investments is included under advance taxes paid.

t: Which of the following is NOT one of the prescribed final-account forms for a general insurer?
e: The three forms are B-RA (Revenue Account), B-PL (Profit and Loss Account) and B-BS (Balance Sheet).

t: Workmen's Compensation / Employer's Liability business is shown:
o: Only if it exceeds 10% of premium
e: WC/Employer's liability is one of the specified segments requiring a separate schedule.

t: Share capital ₹300 crore; securities premium ₹400 crore; general reserve ₹600 crore; revaluation reserve ₹80 crore; FVCA ₹40 crore; accumulated losses ₹50 crore. Shareholders' Funds are:
e: 300 + 400 + 600 − 50 = ₹1,250 crore; revaluation reserve and FVCA are excluded.

t: Section 64VB of the Insurance Act 1938 requires that:
o: Premium is received in advance before the risk is assumed
Every policy carries a free-look clause
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). No risk may be assumed unless the premium has been received in advance or is guaranteed in the manner prescribed.

t: Which of the following is a permitted purpose for a loan or advance to a full-time employee?
o: Loan to a relative of the employee
Purchase of shares of the insurer
e: Festival advance is listed; others are not permitted purposes.

t: 'Other forms of capital' that an insurer may issue under the 2024 Registration and Capital Structure regulations are:
o: Preference share capital and subordinated debt
e: Insurers may raise funds through preference share capital and subordinated debt.

t: Rural sector premium was ₹400 crore in the previous year and ₹600 crore in the current year. The additional allowable expenses of management on this account are:
e: 15% of the incremental rural premium: 15% × (600 − 400) = ₹30 crore.

t: Profit after tax ₹150 crore and net premium ₹3,000 crore. Net earnings ratio is:
e: Net earnings ratio = PAT / net premium = 150 / 3,000 = 5%.
